WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of him

Asa took the silver and gold left in the treasuries of the house of the LORD and of the palace, and sent them “to Ben-hadad, the son of Tabrimon, the son of Hezion, king of Syria, that dwelt at Damascus”. 1 Kings 15:18
Asa's message: “There is a league between me and thee, and between my father and thy father … come and break thy league with Baasha king of Israel, that he may depart from me.” 1 Kings 15:19
“So Ben-hadad hearkened unto king Asa”, and sent his captains against the cities of Israel. 1 Kings 15:20

In 1 Kings 20, “Ben-hadad the king of Syria” besieged Samaria with thirty-two kings, was routed there and again at Aphek, and begged for his life; Ahab made a covenant with him and let him go. 1 Kings 20:1–34
A prophet told Ahab that the LORD had appointed this king “to utter destruction”. 1 Kings 20:42
Jeremiah, of Damascus: “I will kindle a fire in the wall of Damascus, and it shall consume the palaces of Ben-hadad.” Jeremiah 49:27
DEALINGS
Dealings with God's people

His servants said of Israel, “Their gods are gods of the hills”; a man of God answered that the LORD would give the Syrians into Ahab's hand, “and ye shall know that I am the LORD”. 1 Kings 20:23 1 Kings 20:28
A league with Judah: Asa speaks of a league “between me and thee, and between my father and thy father”. 1 Kings 15:19
A league with Baasha of Israel, which he broke for Asa's silver and gold. 1 Kings 15:19–20
A covenant with Ahab after Aphek: “thou shalt make streets for thee in Damascus, as my father made in Samaria”. 1 Kings 20:34
His captains struck the north of Israel, “all the land of Naphtali”. 1 Kings 15:20

Samaria under siege: he claimed its king's silver, gold, wives and children, then swore: “The gods do so unto me, and more also, if the dust of Samaria shall suffice for handfuls for all the people that follow me.” 1 Kings 20:3 1 Kings 20:10

DATES DIFFER
When was it?
PLACED BY SCRIPTURE'S KINGS OF ISRAEL AND JUDAH (THIELE, AS REVISED BY MCFALL AND YOUNG)
No years given[1]

No year of his own is known. His contemporaries in 1 Kings 15 are Asa (912/911–871/870 BC) and Baasha (909/908–886/885 BC). If the Ben-hadad of 1 Kings 20 is the same man, he was still reigning in Ahab's time (874/873–853 BC).
Two men: Asa's Ben-hadad and his son
C. F. Keil (tr. 1872), pp. 221, 261 and 266–267; T. Nicol, ISBE (1915)

Keil counts three kings of Damascus called Ben-hadad: the son of Tabrimon, “his son in the time of Ahab”, and the son of Hazael. He reads the cities taken by Ahab's enemy's father (1 Kings 20:34) as a war with Omri “of which no account has been preserved”. Nicol calls Ahab's opponent Benhadad II, “in all probability the son of Benhadad I”. 1 Kings 20:34 [22][15]
Scripture leaves it open
Our reading of the text

1 Kings 20 never gives Ahab's enemy a father's name. He speaks of cities “which my father took from thy father” and streets his father made in Samaria, while 1 Kings 15 tells only of cities taken from Baasha in Naphtali. 1 Kings 20:34 1 Kings 15:20

WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture gives this Ben-hadad no length of reign, no age, and no account of his death.
1 Kings 15 does not say what Ben-hadad's league with Baasha was, or when it was made.
1 Kings 20 never names the father of the Ben-hadad who besieged Samaria.
Scripture tells of no war between Omri and Damascus, though Ahab's enemy speaks of cities his father took from Ahab's father (1 Kings 20:34).
Scripture does not call Hezion a king, nor say that he is the Rezon of 1 Kings 11.
No Assyrian record used here names a Ben-hadad in Ahab's time; the Monolith names Hadad-ezer.
The “king of Syria” whose captains fought Ahab at Ramoth-gilead (1 Kings 22:31) is not named; that he is this Ben-hadad is a reading, and 1 Kings 22 is not on this page.
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON

From the textThe site's person record for this Ben-hadad holds two passages: Ben-hadad son of Tabrimon, whom Asa paid (1 Kings 15:18–20; 2 Chronicles 16:2–4), and the Ben-hadad who besieged Samaria in Ahab's reign (1 Kings 20). Scripture does not say whether they are one man. This page shows each passage on its own and sets out the question with its holders. 1 Kings 15:18 1 Kings 20:1
From the textHe is not the Ben-hadad of Elisha's day (2 Kings 6:24; 8:7) nor Ben-hadad the son of Hazael (2 Kings 13:24); each has his own page. 2 Kings 6:24 2 Kings 13:24

From the textJeremiah's oracle on Damascus, “it shall consume the palaces of Ben-hadad”, is held on this record. The verse names no king of its own day; it uses the name of Damascus's palaces. Jeremiah 49:27
